preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 1 and line.strip() in {'A', 'B'} for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each test case line contains exactly one string composed solely of 'A' and 'B' characters.
The number of test cases T is between 1 and 10 (inclusive).

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= len(line) <= 5000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each string S has length N where 2 ≤ N ≤ 5000.

postconditions.expression: all((output_line == '-1' and not any(len(T) >= 1 and count_subsequence(S, T) == 2 for T in all_possible_subsequences(S))) or (output_line != '-1' and len(output_line) >= 1 and count_subsequence(S, output_line) == 2)) for S, output_line in zip(stdin.splitlines()[1:], stdout.splitlines()) if output_line != '-1'
postconditions.description: For each test case, if no string T appears exactly twice as a subsequence in S, output '-1'. Otherwise, output a string T that appears exactly twice as a subsequence in S. The function `count_subsequence(S, T)` returns the number of times T appears as a subsequence in S.

postconditions.expression: all(len(output_line) <= len(S) for S, output_line in zip(stdin.splitlines()[1:], stdout.splitlines()) if output_line != '-1')
postconditions.description: The length of the output string T is at most the length of the input string S.
